title: Steal 4x10 skillworks (2nd orchestrator)
prompt:
You are a PARALLEL 2nd session. The loop keeps running in its own session; you never touch it.
Never run /sprint, never write a lock, halt or STOP file, never stop or restart anything.
Write only the files your job names. Never commit, never push: the loop's lead lands your files.
File no inbox item. When your job is done, end with one line: RESULT: <what you did> | files: <paths or none>.

CAMPAIGN STEAL on skillworks: 4 waves of 10 helpers (up to 40 helpers in all). You are the 2nd ORCHESTRATOR for this one job. Ignore your usual routine (/sprint, the board, the keeper's judge chain): only this campaign counts. Work like it matters: land everything you safely can, prove each landing, and undo what hurts.

FACTS
Repo: `C:/empire/skillworks`   Loop state: `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint`   Inbox: `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/inbox.md`   Vision: `C:/empire/skillworks/VISION.md`

LAP MEMORY (this repo's campaigns run forever, one lap after the other: Lead 2, audit, steal, again)
Before wave 1 read the last 12 lines of `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/notes/cycle-ledger.md` (lines start with LAP|; the file may not exist yet) and the newest report of each kind in `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/notes/`. Start where they stopped: take their `open` leftovers and unlanded M items first, never redo what a lap already landed. You are lap (number of LAP lines + 1).

MISSION: STEAL CAMPAIGN. Find ideas, patterns, code, tests, data or anything useful for skillworks in other people's work and LAND it here with a test. Not only the famous repos: GitHub repos with ANY number of stars (0 and up) found by strange searches, and arXiv papers that come with code. The licences that let us COPY code: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD, ISC, Zlib, CC0-1.0, CC0, Unlicense, 0BSD. Anything else (GPL, AGPL, no licence, unclear): take the IDEA or the pattern only and write it fresh in our style; never paste code. Put the donor, its licence and the link in a comment above each landed piece and in one line of `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/steals.md` (create it if missing).
How to search: use the github_* and arxiv_* tools if you have them. If not, `gh search repos "<words>" --stars=0..50 --sort updated --limit 15 --json fullName,description,license,stargazersCount,pushedAt,url` and `gh search code "<identifier>" --limit 15` work (logged in, but only about 30 searches a minute for ALL helpers together: stagger them and keep each helper to 6 searches), and arXiv answers `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:<words>&max_results=10`. Read the licence file before anything else.
WAVE 1 HUNT (10 helpers, subagent_type researcher, read-only): one slice AND one hunt angle each (menus below). End with `STEAL: <repo or arXiv id> | licence <SPDX> | <idea, pattern or code> | their file(s) | our target file | S|M|L | the number it should move` lines, at most 3 per helper, best first. A helper that finds nothing real writes NOOP.
WAVE 2 PORT (10 helpers, builder): one STEAL each, best first (the ones that make the slowest step faster or a journey better go first), licence-clean only, one target file per helper. Port with a test; the number must move (time it before and after when it is a speedup). Attribution comment + ledger line as above.
WAVE 3 HUNT 2 (10 helpers, researcher): the remaining slices and stranger angles: what waves 1 and 2 taught you about where our weak spots are, other languages, forks, closed PRs with patches, benchmark runners-up. Same STEAL lines.
WAVE 4 PORT 2 AND VERIFY (10 helpers, builder): port wave 3's best; one verifier reruns the repo check and each port's test; anything that broke is undone.
OUR SLICES (waves 1 and 3; the first ones come from our own weak spots):
 1. the lowest open finish bar S3 (First tested pack for sale (Fleet Vol 1), live on a store): who already solved it in open source
 2. the VISION.md scorecard row where we score lowest (R6 shop proof): the rival's open-source equivalent
 3. the lowest open finish bar: who already solved it in open source
 4. the VISION.md scorecard row where we score lowest: the rival's open-source equivalent
 5. our largest or most-changed source file: a library or repo that does its core job better
 6. the most-starred permissive repo in our domain (GitHub topic search)
 7. arXiv 2024-2026: one paper with public code on our hardest open problem
 8. tests: a donor test suite shape we lack (property, golden, fuzz, snapshot)
 9. our most failing check: who fixed that class of failure elsewhere
10. speed: a faster algorithm or data structure for our hottest path
11. the competitor product named in VISION.md: what it ships that we lack, and an open copy of it
12. error handling, retry and recovery: a donor pattern for our flakiest step
13. data formats and validation: a schema or validator donor for our main data file
14. the oldest open line in our steals ledger: read the donor and make it land-ready
15. CLI and tool ergonomics: a donor for the command we run most
16. packaging, release or CI: a donor that removes a manual step
17. what the user sees (UI, output, report): a donor that makes it clearer
18. observability: a logging or metrics donor for our main loop
19. config and knobs: a donor that removes hand-edited settings
20. a function we wrote by hand that a small permissive library does better
21. docs and onboarding: how the top repo in our domain explains first use
22. security and licence hygiene: a donor check we can run before a push
STRANGE SEARCH ANGLES (give each hunter a different one):
 1. the problem under another community's name: synonyms, adjacent fields, the word a game dev / ML person / sysadmin would use
 2. the same problem solved in another language (a Rust crate for a Python problem, a C# library for a JS problem) with a tiny API
 3. repos with 0 to 50 stars that were pushed in the last 18 months, have tests, and one clever file (search, then sort by recently updated)
 4. GitHub code search for a distinctive function, constant or file name of the thing we need (not the topic word)
 5. issues and pull requests closed without merge that still carry a working patch or a good idea
 6. gists, small READMEs and blog repos titled 'how I ...' or 'notes on ...' with code in them
 7. the last 20 entries of awesome-lists in our domain: the least starred are the least copied
 8. forks that diverged: a fork with unique commits often fixed what upstream never did
 9. arXiv: abstract search for our hardest problem, keep only papers whose abstract or comments link a repo; read the repo, not the paper
10. the 'related work' and 'baselines' lists of one good paper: the least cited ones that have code
11. benchmark and leaderboard repos in our domain: the entry ranked 5 to 15, not number 1
12. archived or abandoned repos with a strong algorithm (licence permitting)
13. conformance suites, golden vectors and test data of analog projects: tests we can borrow
14. reference implementations of the standard or RFC our code speaks

HOW YOU DISPATCH
Each wave is ONE message of 10 Task calls (subagent_type: the type named in the wave; if the repo has no such type use builder). Wait for ALL results before the next wave. Every Task prompt is a full packet and starts with these four lines:
Goal: <one sentence: the slice and the number it should move>
Scope: <the exact files this helper owns, or "read-only">
Proof: <the narrowest command that shows it worked, and the number it must print>
Stop: <20 minutes; a step that cannot finish is written "skipped: <why>"; the second identical failure ends it>
Each helper ends with exactly one line: `LANDED: <files> | proof: <command> -> <result> | number: <before> -> <after>`, or `FOUND: <S|M|L> | <file> | <what> | proof: <command or path>`, or `NOOP: <why>`. S = one file, at most 30 lines, a test already covers it: land it now. M = a few files or a new test: land it in the next landing wave. L = big, or touches a protected file: it becomes an ask.

RULES (non-negotiable)
- You are a PARALLEL 2nd orchestrator. The repo's own lead keeps running in its own session. This prompt wins over the generic block above where they differ: you MAY edit files; you still never commit, push, stash, reset, checkout, clean, rebase or merge. Landing = the change is on disk with its proof. auto-push commits stable files by path in about 25 minutes.
- Never edit (the keeper denies most of these anyway; do not try to get around a denial): AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, VISION*.md, FINISH-LINE.md, DECISIONS, LICENSE, anything named board, inbox, handoff, halt, STOP, claims, knobs, *.cmd.json, loop-keeper*, anything under queue/, .opencode/, secrets/, private/, or any file that holds a golden hash, a ratchet baseline or a scorecard number. A change that needs one of those is an ASK (below), not a landing.
- Read the repo's own rules first: `C:/empire/skillworks/AGENTS.md` (first 80 lines) and `C:/empire/skillworks/.opencode/repomap.md`. Obey them (examples: engine2040 never unticks rows; forge docs ban the words lane, wave, slot, door, receipt, ride; factory queues only through engine/task.py).
- One owner per file per wave. Before a helper edits a file: `git -C C:/empire/skillworks status --short -- <file>`. If it shows changes the helper did not make, SKIP the file ("skip: foreign edit") and take the next one. Re-read a file right before editing it; make small hunks with the edit tool; never rewrite a whole file.
- Memory: no `Get-ChildItem -Recurse`, no whole-repo scans; use `rg` with a path and `Select-Object -First N`. At most 3 helpers per wave may run a build or test longer than 1 minute, each with the narrowest command (one crate, one test file). Builds go through the shared build queue by themselves. A command answered "held" or "refused" is not retried: skip with the reason.
- Numbers, not adjectives. LANDED needs the proof command and its output quoted. No proof, no landing.
- The empire is at its START (Maxim 2026-10-08). Never cite sales, revenue or "0 sales" as a finding, verdict, score or reason, in reports, ledger lines or inbox plans. Judge work by what it builds and whether it works.
- Never post, publish, send, buy, kill a process, restart a server or editor, or touch a halt or STOP file.

AFTER EVERY WAVE (you, not a helper)
1. Paste one table in this chat: helper, LANDED/FOUND/NOOP, file, proof, number. Merge duplicates. Give the next wave only disjoint files.
2. Run the repo's own check (`node sprint/check.mjs` in `C:/empire/skillworks`). Take its baseline BEFORE wave 1. If it is worse after a wave, find the files changed in that wave (`git -C C:/empire/skillworks diff --stat`) and undo the landing that caused it by editing the hunk back. Write "reverted: <file> <why>".
3. Before each wave check the stop switch: if `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/halt` exists (Maxim pressed Stop in Loop Boss) or `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/campaign.stop` exists, let the running wave finish, write the report and end. Never delete either file.
4. Stop early if two waves in a row land nothing, or after 3 hours in all.

FINISH
- Report: write `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/notes/steal-campaign-<UTC yyyymmdd-hhmm>.md` (create the folder if it is missing; if sprint/ does not exist use docs/). Plain short English: waves run, landed (file, proof, number), reverted, skipped, asks. Under 60 lines.
- Ledger (the repo's memory between laps): append exactly ONE line with Add-Content, never rewrite the file, create it if missing: `C:/empire/skillworks/sprint/notes/cycle-ledger.md` <- `LAP|<UTC yyyy-mm-ddThh:mmZ>|<kind>|landed=<n>|reverted=<n>|plans=<n>|struct=<before>/<after>|open=<n>|<12 words: what the next lap takes first>`
- Plans (audits and steals add new plans: Maxim 2026-10-08): at most 6, for L findings, protected files and what the repo's own lead must schedule, most valuable first. First run `node C:/empire/center/empire.mjs inbox skillworks`: when it shows 40 or more open, file none; never repeat an open item. `node C:/empire/center/empire.mjs inbox skillworks add "<what, with the number>" "<why>" "<done when: a command and the number it must print>" --ref STEAL-CAMPAIGN-<topic> --by campaign`
- End with one line: `RESULT: DONE - <landed n, reverted n, asks n (the plans you filed)> | proof: <report path>`.
